Executive assessment

The original review found six UI issues and five code risks. The 25 September implementation addresses those findings, excluding NEVO attribution by request. On iPhone 18 Pro 2, the new Combo action, single-name food form, inline validation, and immediate serving selection after saving were visually confirmed. The cached development client now runs the current JavaScript bundle on iPhone 18 Pro 2, allowing the remaining screen checks.

Implementation update

The food forms now omit repeated titles and use one personal-food name. The empty Combo screen starts diary selection, the saved-food row opens serving details immediately, and validation appears beside the name field. Library restore, upload retry, offline settings, barcode error cleanup, and user-facing sync errors were also addressed in code.

Evidence labels matter: “Observed” means reproduced on the simulator; “Code risk” means the path was identified by reading code and still needs a controlled failure test. The original 23 September review was read-only; the 25 September implementation status appears below.

Original reproduced findings

These cards describe the 23 September device state. Their implementation status is recorded above.

P2Observed

Food forms show a redundant title in a crowded header

On the 402 px wide simulator, the title is compressed between “Annuleren” and “Persoonlijk voedingsmiddel opslaan” and breaks into isolated letters. The issue appears in personal-food creation and Open Food Facts review.

Code: form.tsx:71 · personal-food-editor-form.tsx:527

Decision: Remove the duplicate title from the food editor header. The creation tab already names the type; import context can sit in the form body. Keep Cancel and Save readable on narrow screens.

P2Observed

New personal food cannot be selected until the picker is reopened

After saving a new food, it appeared in picker search, but tapping its row repeatedly did not show serving details. Leaving the picker and reopening it made the same row work. The food itself was stored correctly.

Code: nutrition-food-browser.tsx:733

Fix: Coordinate editor dismissal with presenting the serving sheet, then cover that exact iOS interaction with a regression test.

P2Observed

Personal-food naming and validation need one clear field

Saving an empty personal-food form left the view at the top with no visible error. The error appeared only after scrolling to the bottom: “Food name English is required and must be at most 500 characters.” The form also exposes a separate English-name field, although a personal food should have one name across app languages.

Code: personal-food-editor-form.tsx:378 and :866

Decision: Show one personal-food name field, use that name across app languages, localize validation, and scroll or focus the invalid field. The storage representation can be adapted behind the form.

P3Observed

One-off logging repeats the form title

The header displayed “Eenmalig logg…” beside the save action while “Eenmalig” was already selected in the form tabs. The rest of the form remained usable.

Decision: Omit the repeated title and keep the selected tab as the form context.

P3Observed

Empty states do not clearly guide the next action

The empty food picker says “Nog niets om te loggen” although it offers search across 2,393 foods. The empty Combo screen explains that entries must be selected in the diary but offers no direct action to start that selection.

Copy: nutrition-food-browser-copy.ts:156 · UI: nutrition-combos.tsx:561

Decision: Clarify the picker wording and add a plus action to the Combo empty state that starts selecting diary items.

P3Observed

Assistance mode label is clipped

“Voedingsschatting” renders as “Voedingsschat…” in the three-way selector on this iPhone. Its accessibility label remains complete.

Fix: Use shorter visible labels or a mode selector with enough width for Dutch text.

Original code risks

P2Code risk

Library restore depends on opening settings

Paging the server library happens in the settings screen rather than at the library provider level. A user who never opens settings, or leaves before all pages complete, may see an incomplete personal library on that device.

nutrition-library.tsx:84 · personal-foods.tsx:256

P2Code risk

Transient library upload failure has no scheduled retry

The failed operation is requeued, but no timer schedules the next attempt while the connection remains up. It may wait for another trigger or manual retry.

nutrition-library-service.ts:252

P2Code risk

Settings can remain a skeleton while offline

When backup is enabled and the server query is unresolved, settings returns the loading view. Offline text appears below the skeleton, but local controls are not available in that state.

nutrition-library.tsx:204

P3Code risk

Barcode lookup may retain loading after an unexpected rejection

The lookup sets loading before awaiting the request and clears it only on normal completion. A rejected promise has no finally cleanup in this handler.

nutrition-food-browser.tsx:633

P3Code risk

Sync failure exposes raw error text

The status screen prints operation.lastError, which may be technical or untranslated rather than a user action.

nutrition-sync-status.tsx:38

Remaining verification

The review did not verify a physical barcode scan, second-device restore, forced network failures, Android, VoiceOver, saved goal changes, completed Open Food Facts import, photo handling, or every Combo and assistance mutation. The automated suite covers many of those paths, but a simulator pass cannot prove them all.

  1. Repeat the changed screen checks with large text and make a fresh native development-client build when Apple signing is available.
  2. Exercise a physical barcode scan, second-device restore, and controlled offline transitions.
  3. Complete the remaining import, Combo, assistance, photo, and VoiceOver flows that the original review marked partial.

The temporary test food created during the 25 September simulator check was removed. Other workspace changes are outside this nutrition follow-up.
